name: How does Denver's dry climate affect interior wood trim and baseboards?

mainEntity.name: How does Denver's dry climate affect interior wood trim and baseboards?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the greater Denver metro area, the semi-arid climate and seasonal temperature shifts cause homes to experience significant indoor humidity swings. Rapid humidity drops cause wood and MDF trim to contract, leading to hairline cracks at miter joints or caulked edges. Finish carpenters in communities like Centennial, Parker, and Greenwood Village acclimate trim materials inside the home prior to installation. Using flexible, high-grade acrylic caulking and coped inside corners rather than simple miter cuts helps joints stay tight as seasons change.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry air causes wood contraction and joint gaps; letting trim acclimate indoors and using coped joints with flexible caulk prevents winter cracking.
